title: Perfect state transfer and Cayley presentations
abstract: We study perfect state transfer on Cayley graphs from the point of view that state transfer is a property of a graph and not of a group. This paper is a bridge between the classical question about isomorphic Cayley graphs of non-isomorphic groups and quantum walks on graphs.   We show that a Cayley graph of a group with an abelian subgroup of index two is a Cayley graph of an abelian group under any one of three hypotheses, two drawn from the theory of isomorphic Cayley graphs. A statement of the same kind holds for extraspecial groups: every Cayley graph of an extraspecial $p$-group of order $p^{2n+1}$ with a conjugacy-closed connection set is a Cayley graph of $Z_p^{2n+1}$. From these results we deduce that every explicit construction of perfect state transfer in the six papers we survey, on dihedral, dicyclic, generalized dihedral, $V_{8n}$ and extraspecial $2$-groups, is a non-abelian presentation of an abelian Cayley graph. Moreover, we show that a non-abelian group with an abelian subgroup of index two admits a connected Cayley graph with perfect state transfer if and only if its order is divisible by four.   Genuinely non-abelian examples do exist. We prove that, for every odd prime power $q\ge 5$, the $SL(2,q)$ graph of Pantangi and Sin, which they showed to admit perfect state transfer, is a Cayley graph of no abelian group; to our knowledge, this is the first infinite family of Cayley graphs with perfect state transfer provably admitting no abelian Cayley presentation. We also construct an infinite family of Cayley graphs with peak state transfer and determine all regular subgroups of the automorphism group of every member.   An appendix records a census of the connected vertex-transitive graphs with perfect state transfer on at most $30$ vertices.
summary: This work investigates Perfect State Transfer (PST) in quantum walks on graphs, treating it as a property of the graph structure rather than just the underlying group. The authors provide deep results linking PST to the algebraic structure of the graph's automorphism group, proving that many known examples are non-abelian presentations of abelian graphs, while also constructing new infinite families that definitively require non-abelian group structures.
main_problem: The paper bridges the classical graph theory problem of isomorphic Cayley graphs with the quantum physics concept of Perfect State Transfer (PST) in quantum walks.
main_result: It establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for a non-abelian group to admit a Cayley graph with PST, and provides an infinite family of such graphs that cannot be presented as Cayley graphs of any abelian group.
method: The analysis combines spectral graph theory (for PST detection) with advanced group theory (using theorems like Sabidussi's) to characterize the automorphism groups of the graphs.
model_or_system: The model is quantum walks on graphs, where the dynamics are governed by the adjacency matrix $A$ of a graph $X$, and the physical observable is the probability amplitude for state transfer between vertices.
key_observables: Perfect State Transfer (PST) at time $	au$, defined by $|U(	au)_{v,u}| = 1$, and the spectrum of the adjacency matrix $A$.
important_parameters: The order of the group $|G|$, the index of abelian subgroups, and the prime power $q$ defining the $	ext{SL}(2, q)$ graphs.
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on the graph being a Cayley graph $	ext{Cay}(G, S)$ and the application of theorems relating graph automorphisms to group structure.
figures_summary: The paper includes a census of connected vertex-transitive graphs with PST on at most 30 vertices, and large tables summarizing parameters, spectra, and associated Cayley groups for numerous graphs.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing general conditions for PST in Cayley graphs, then proving results for specific families (like those related to abelian subgroups of index two), and finally constructing and analyzing infinite families of counterexamples (like the $	ext{SL}(2, q)$ graphs) to show non-abelian presentations.
why_interesting: The connection between algebraic structure (group theory) and quantum dynamics (quantum walks) is highly relevant to understanding the robustness and limitations of quantum information processing on physical architectures modeled by graphs.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Two graphs with perfect state transfer, each of which is a Cayley graph of every group of its order. They are rows X8c (left) and X12a (right) of the census in Ap- pendix A. They are drawn in their circulant presentations, X8c = Cay(Z8, {±1, ±3, 4}) and X12a = Cay(Z12, {±1, ±2, ±4, ±5, 6}), and in both the perfect state transfer at time π/2 is between the vertices x and x + n/2 connected by orange edges.

Figure 2. The 24-vertex counterexample X = Cay(S4, S). Edges are coloured by generator: the transposition (1 2) gives the orange perfect matching, the other four transpositions are grey, and the four 3-cycles are blue. Perfect state transfer at time π/2 occurs between vertices connected by the orange perfect matching. The graph is row X24b of the census (Appendix A).

Figure 5. Illustration of the twin reduction. If every twin class of X has size two and distinct classes are joined by all four possible edges or by none, then X is the lexicographic product Y [K2] (adjacent classes, as drawn) or Y [2K1] (non-adjacent classes) of the quotient graph Y over the classes. For the graphs of [35] the classes are the pairs {g, tg} with t = −I (Lemma 6.5, Appendix B), perfect state transfer runs from g to tg inside each class (orange), and Aut(X) = C2 ≀Aut(Y ) by Lemma 6.4.
